name: mettaur-attack-compare
label: The Mettaur's whole 70-frame attack cycle, real ROM left and this build right: 0.0 pixels a frame. It hides, swings, and sends a shockwave down the row. The virus acts on an RNG neither side shares, so there is no fixed offset to compare on -- the two are aligned by finding the lag that lines up the frames on which its own bounding box changes, and 16 of the real side's 17 boundaries land exactly. This was the last animated residue: it fell from 460 pixels to 345 when a hop turned out to spawn a new segment rather than move one, and from 345 to 0 when the segment left behind turned out to be destroyed a frame too early.

name: battle-opening
label: How a battle opens in the build now: white held and ramped off, the field, the virus materialising, the chip window. The lead-in was 32 frames of black where the real ROM is 71 of white plus a 16-frame ramp, and with that one constant wrong everything after it looked wrong in its own way. Fixing it aligned all of them: the virus starts materialising at frame 76 and settles at 142 on both sides, and the chip window opens at 130 against 129.

name: full-battle-loop
label: A whole battle end to end in the rollup ROM: the chip window a battle opens with, the BATTLE START! ribbon, the fight, the win, the RESULT window with its reward, and into the next battle's chip select. This loop did not exist before today -- the release build fielded four enemies that delete the navi in fifteen seconds and started the custom gauge empty, 1260 frames before the first chip. Every piece here is separately matched to the real ROM pixel for pixel.

name: battle-open-compare
label: How a battle opens, real ROM above and this build below. Found with the harness's first save state at a battle's FIRST frame, which immediately showed two things wrong here: a battle OPENS with the chip window (frame 165, unprompted) where this build made you wait 1260 frames for it, and BATTLE START! follows the chip window rather than the intro. Corrected, the banner lands at 291 against the real ROM's 292.

name: wave-departure-compare
label: The Mettaur's shockwave, real ROM left and this build right. A hop is not one sprite moving: the real ROM spawns a whole new segment on the next panel and the old one stops where it is, playing out its own animation until it comes back round to its last frame. The residue had been recorded as the virus holding its pickaxe too long -- its body is 0 pixels across all 70 frames. Now at 0: the last three frames were the departing segment being destroyed the instant its animation reached its final frame, rather than after that frame had been held for the duration it asks for -- the real ROM's own "last frame" flag is masked off until the frame's duration counter runs out, so it never means "reached", only "finished".

name: cursor-compare
label: The chip-select cursor walking OK to the fifth slot, real ROM left and this build right: 170 frames, 0 pixels. Everything the script drives -- the cursor, the card, the name -- was exact for a long time while the highlight bracket's blink stayed one frame out, and that was written off as unfixable: the blink counts from the window's opening, the real side is a save state already open, so the two clocks were said to have no shared origin. Reading the routine instead of guessing at it settled it. The phase is (counter >> 3) & 1 off a frame counter in the window's own struct, window-relative on both sides -- the save state's value simply is not zero. The missing frame turned out to be ours: our slide-in reached its open state one frame after the real ROM's does, invisible everywhere except in that blink.

name: banner-compare
label: The ENEMY DELETED banner, real ROM above and this build below: 0 pixels over all 58 frames. The banner is text -- a font of 8x16 cells and a record per message, twenty cells uploaded as five 32x16 objects -- and all forty-five of the game's messages are in the build. The unrolling is one shared affine matrix whose vertical scale opens from a flat line, overshoots into a stretch, holds and rolls back up.
